```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "A shows money already moving. Cole County, MO paid $7,000 for a compliance tool in March 2026. CivicPlus/AudioEye quoted Templeton, MA $2,510. GovAccess ($149/month) and CASO Comply ($0.30/page) publish prices. Each figure is sourced. B's price anchors are also sourced, but its only evidence of buyers paying is the competitors' own price pages.",
    "A has a specific, sourced reason to buy: dated federal compliance deadlines (April 2027 and April 2028), cited to ADA.gov and the Federal Register. B has no comparable forcing event.",
    "B's own brief cites 100% churn of paying customers on a closely related SaaS. It also cites Dinolingo reviews describing children 'zoning out' during repetitive content. Both point at the core mechanic, not just the build quality.",
    "B's demand evidence is very thin: one Reddit parent who says 'there are so many options' (which signals saturation), plus marketing copy from a competitor. A has two on-record quotes from county officials at an entity that actually spent money.",
    "Both ideas carry compliance risk. A's liability exposure is real, but a scanner-only MVP at around $149/month can sit below formal procurement thresholds. B's COPPA/GDPR-K voice-recording obligations apply on day one of any MVP that records children.",
    "B's consumer subscription model needs ongoing volume at a $4.70 CPI, or influencer spend, to matter, and its churn signal undercuts that. For A, a single small municipality paying $149/month is a credible 90-day win."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's second demand quote ('The existing apps weren't helping our kids make friends or speak with confidence') is founder marketing copy from Voiczy, a direct competitor. It is not independent evidence of unmet demand, and it mainly shows the niche is already taken by an identically positioned product.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A has real weaknesses. Municipal procurement speed and solo-vendor insurance and reference requirements are unanswered, and they threaten the 90-day target directly. The conference booth pricing comes from a 2015 prospectus. The Cole County quotes express resentment of the mandate and a tendency to delete content rather than eagerness to buy. The deadline has already been extended once. Even so, B's documented churn, its absence of any spend evidence beyond published competitor prices, and its child-data compliance burden make it the clearly weaker bet."
}
```
